context:
Use ast module to find @pytest.mark.skip(if), @pytest.mark.xfail decorators
and inline pytest.skip()/pytest.xfail() calls. For each, capture the
condition expression and reason kwarg.

Triage rule of thumb: if you can't explain in one sentence why this test is
skipped, either improve the reason or remove the test.
description:
Quality plan Phase 4d. The audit found 276 skip/xfail markers across the
test suite. Many are legitimate (conditional on optional deps like PYSPARK,
CUDA, etc.) but there is no audit trail establishing that. Quietly-dead
tests can mask real failures and rot over time as the underlying conditions
change.

Triage every skip/xfail. Each must have either:
  1. A `reason=` string referencing an issue/ticket, OR
  2. A condition that's clearly self-explanatory (e.g., `not PYSPARK_AVAILABLE`)
     AND a comment explaining why this test exists if PySpark is the only
     way to validate it
  3. Removal if no longer relevant

anti_patterns.dont: make the warning into an error

preserves.behavior: Skip conditions for optional dependencies remain functional (don't break PYSPARK_AVAILABLE-style guards)
Test count unchanged unless removal is explicitly justified

verifications.description: Audit script runs and produces inventory
All tests still pass (no regressions from edits)
Conftest warning fires on a synthetic skip without reason

work_units.summary: Generate inventory: scripts/audit_skip_xfail.py walks tests/, emits CSV with (file, line, marker_type, condition, current_reason)
Triage inventory in batches by directory: tests/unit/platforms/, tests/unit/core/, tests/integration/ - for each, decide keep/improve/remove
Apply changes - improve reasons, remove dead skips, file follow-up TODOs for any xfail that should become passing
Add a pytest plugin or conftest hook that warns on skip/xfail without reason= (don't fail - would be too disruptive - warn only)
